article.title: Adapting to the effects of climate change

items.sentence_raw: All around the world, nations are already preparing for, and adapting to, climate change and its impacts.

Even if we stopped all CO2 emissions tomorrow, we would continue to see the impact of the CO2 already released since industrial times, with scientists forecasting that global warming would continue for around 40 years.
items.explain: Q15: The passage in this paragraph says scientists forecast *'global warming would continue for around 40 years'*. **'forecast'** means **'prediction'**, and **'continue for around 40 years'** is how long climate change effects will last. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: In the meantime, ice caps would continue to melt and sea levels rise.
Some countries and regions will suffer more extreme impacts from these changes than others.
It's in these places that innovation is thriving.
In Miami Beach, Florida, USA, seawater isn't just breaching the island city's walls, it's seeping up through the ground, so the only way to save the city is to lift it up above sea level.
Starting in the lowest and most vulnerable neighbourhoods, roads have been raised by as much as 61 centimetres.
The elevation work was carried out as part of Miami Beach's ambitious but much-needed stormwater-management programme.
items.explain: Q18: The passage says Miami Beach's stormwater-management programme added *'new pumps that can remove up to 75,000 litres of water per minute'*. These pumps are very efficient. So the answer is **pumps**.

items.sentence_raw: In addition to the road adaptations, the city has set up new pumps that can remove up to 75,000 litres of water per minute.
items.explain: Q18: The passage says Miami Beach's stormwater-management programme added *'new pumps that can remove up to 75,000 litres of water per minute'*. These pumps are very efficient. So the answer is **pumps**.

items.sentence_raw: In the face of floods, climate-mitigation strategies have often been overlooked, says Yanira Pineda, a senior sustainability coordinator.
She knows that they're essential and that the job is far from over.
items.explain: Q25: Yanira Pineda says *'in 20, 30, 40 years, we'll need to go back in there and adjust to the changing environment'*. **'in 20, 30, 40 years'** means **'future decades'**. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: "We know that in 20, 30, 40 years, we'll need to go back in there and adjust to the changing environment," she says.
items.explain: Q25: Yanira Pineda says *'in 20, 30, 40 years, we'll need to go back in there and adjust to the changing environment'*. **'in 20, 30, 40 years'** means **'future decades'**. So the answer is **A**.

items.sentence_raw: Seawalls are a staple strategy for many coastal communities, but on the soft, muddy northern shores of Java, Indonesia, they frequently collapse, further exacerbating coastal erosion.

There have been many attempts to restore the island's coastal mangroves: ecosystems of trees and shrubs that help defend coastal areas by trapping sediment in their net-like root systems, elevating the sea bed and dampening the energy of waves and tidal currents.
items.explain: Q14: The passage in this paragraph says *'mangroves: ecosystems of trees and shrubs that help defend coastal areas'*. **'mangroves'** are a type of plant, and **'defend coastal areas'** means **'natural protection for coastlines'**. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: But Susanna Tol of the not-for-profit organisation Wetlands International says that, while hugely popular, the majority of mangrove-planting projects fail.

So, Wetlands International started out with a different approach, building semi-permeable dams, made from bamboo poles and brushwood, to mimic the role of mangrove roots and create favourable conditions for mangroves to grow back naturally.
items.explain: Q19: The passage says Wetlands International first built *'semi-permeable dams'* to create good conditions for mangroves to grow. **'first stage of a project'** matches the start of this approach. So the answer is **dams**.

items.sentence_raw: The programme has seen moderate success, mainly in areas with less subsidence.
"Unfortunately, traditional infrastructure is often single-solution focused," says Tol.
"For long-term success, it's critical that we transition towards multifunctional approaches that embed natural processes and that engage and benefit communities and local decision-makers."
items.explain: Q23: Susanna Tol says successful approaches must *'engage and benefit communities'*. **'engage and benefit communities'** means **'involve and help residents of the region'**. So the answer is **B**.

items.sentence_raw: As the floodwaters rose in the rice fields of the Mekong Delta in September 2018, four small houses rose with them.
Homes in this part of Vietnam are traditionally built on stilts but these ones had been built to float.
items.explain: Q20: The passage says the Buoyant Foundation Project made houses *'to float'* for the Mekong Delta. These houses rise with floodwaters. So the answer is **float**.

items.sentence_raw: The modifications were made by the Buoyant Foundation Project, a not-for-profit organisation that has been researching and retrofitting amphibious houses since 2006.
items.explain: Q20: The passage says the Buoyant Foundation Project made houses *'to float'* for the Mekong Delta. These houses rise with floodwaters. So the answer is **float**.

items.sentence_raw: "When I started this," explains founder Elizabeth English, "climate change was not on the tip of everybody's tongue, but this technology is becoming necessary in places that didn't previously need it."
items.explain: Q26: Elizabeth English says the floating house technology *'is becoming necessary in places that didn't previously need it'*. **'places that didn't previously need it'** means the number of locations needing flood action has grown. So the answer is **C**.

items.sentence_raw: It's much cheaper than permanently elevating houses, English explains - about a third of what it would cost to completely replace a building's foundations.
items.explain: Q16: The passage in this paragraph says the floating house technology *'is much cheaper than permanently elevating houses'*. **'much cheaper'** means **'cost-effective'**. So the answer is **D**.

items.sentence_raw: It also avoids the problem of taller houses being at greater risk from wind damage.
Another plus comes from the fact that amphibious structures can be sensitively adapted to meet cultural needs and match the kind of houses that are already common in a community.
Bangladesh is especially vulnerable to climate change.
Most of the country is less than a metre above sea level and 80 per cent of its land lies on floodplains.

"Almost 35 million people living on the coastal belt of Bangladesh are currently affected by soil and water salinity," says Raisa Chowdhury of the international development organisation ICCO Cooperation.
Rather than fighting against it, one project is helping communities adapt to salt-affected soils.
ICCO Cooperation has been working with 10,000 farmers in Bangladesh to start cultivating naturally salt-tolerant crops in the region.
items.explain: Q21: The passage says Bangladesh is introducing *'naturally salt-tolerant crops'* for high-salt areas. **'salt-tolerant'** means **'suitable for areas of high salt content'**. So the answer is **crops**.

items.sentence_raw: Certain varieties of carrot, potato, kohlrabi, cabbage and beetroot have been found to be better suited to salty soil than the rice and wheat that is typically grown there.

Chowdhury says that the results are very visible, comparing a barren plot of land to the 'beautiful, lush green vegetable garden' sitting beside it, in which she and her team have been working with the farmers.
Since the project began, farmers trained in saline agriculture have reported increases of two to three more harvests per year.
Greg Spotts from Los Angeles (LA) in the USA is chief sustainability officer of the city's street services department.

He leads the Cool Streets LA programme, a series of pilot projects, which include the planting of trees and the installation of a 'cool pavement' system, designed to help reach the city's goal of bringing down its average temperature by 1.5°C.
items.explain: Q22: The passage says the Cool Streets LA programme includes *'the planting of trees'* on city streets. So the answer is **trees**.

items.sentence_raw: "Urban cooling is literally a matter of life and death for our future in LA," says Spotts.
items.explain: Q24: Greg Spotts says *'Urban cooling is literally a matter of life and death for our future in LA'*. **'matter of life and death'** means **'absolutely vital for our survival'**. So the answer is **E**.

items.sentence_raw: Using a Geographic Information System data mapping tool, the programme identified streets with low tree canopy cover in three of the city's neighbourhoods and covered them with a light-grey, light-reflecting coating, which had already been shown to lower road surface temperature in Los Angeles by 6°C.
items.explain: Q17: The passage in this paragraph says *'Using a Geographic Information System data mapping tool, the programme identified streets with low tree canopy cover'*. **'Geographic Information System data mapping tool'** is a **technology to locate areas that need help**. So the answer is **F**.

items.sentence_raw: Spotts says one of these streets, in the Winnetka neighbourhood of San Fernando Valley, can now be seen as a pale crescent, the only cool spot on an otherwise red thermal image, from the International Space Station.
